precepts.text: All Israel in like manner cried most earnestly unto the Lord, because their death was before their eyes. That is when our people are going to come: when death is before their eyes, they will cry earnestly and look for God. And when they come, we will show them how to get right.
precepts.point: News discussed in class: the hands of the civil rights era are being turned back right now. Memphis, one of the blackest cities in America, has been carved up by gerrymandering and parceled out to the outskirts of the state so that its people cannot win a congressional seat any more; it is happening in Texas and everywhere. An elected black congressman was hauled out by state troopers protesting that he was lawfully there. We frame the law by mischief is written for a reason. Our people swear they are going to vote their way out of this, and the churches that once organized the community are silent. Where is the Christian church on the front line while all of this is turned back, while our people are found hanged in 2026 and it is ruled suicide? The only ones crying aloud about it are the Israelites. The teaching stands: our people need to see the affliction for what it is, get their minds right, and get lined up on the right side before the decree brings forth.

note.label: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.why:
“in their affliction they will seek me early.” God returns to his place, and our people have to seek him, but they have to be afflicted first. That is how our people are. And the afflictions are just starting. We have been getting killed in the street by police, but that ain't it; that is only the prelude to what is about to happen.

Esau is turning back the hands of the civil rights era right now, and that is good, because black people trust in their oppression. Memphis, maybe the blackest city in America, has been gerrymandered and carved up and parcelled out to the outskirts of the state so no black man can win a congressional seat there anymore, and it is happening in Texas and everywhere. An elected black congressman was hauled out by state troopers, protesting that he was an elected official and lawfully there. White guilt is out the window. Our people swear they are going to vote their way out of this, and they need the affliction, to see the devil for who he is.

In Esther's day: “All Israel in like manner cried most earnestly unto the Lord, because their death was before their eyes.” That is when our people are going to come: when death is before their eyes, they will cry earnestly and look for God. Right now they are still confused about who the devil is.

The church that once organized the community and planned the votes is silent while the civil rights laws are turned back, while our people are found hanged in 2026 with their organs taken out and it is called suicide. The only ones crying out about it are the Israelites. So it is our job to warn our people and bring them to repentance, and when they come with death before their eyes, we will show them what they are doing wrong and how to get right.

precepts.text: Mordecai's own prayer shows he refused to bow not from contempt but so as not to set the glory of man above the glory of the Most High.
precepts.point: The servants asked daily why Mordecai transgressed the king's commandment, and he hearkened not, but told them he was a Jew, and they told Haman to see whether Mordecai's matter would stand. We do not bow, the same as the three Hebrew children did not bow to the image in Babylon, for we pledge allegiance to none but the Most High.

note.label: Esther 3: Haman the Agagite and the Decree to Destroy the Jews

precepts.why:
“Mordecai bowed not, nor did him reverence.” The servants asked him daily why he transgressed the king's commandment, and he told them he was a Jew. His own prayer in the Apocrypha gives the reason from the inside: “thou knowest, Lord, that it was neither in contempt nor pride, nor for any desire of glory, that I did not bow down to proud Aman. For I could have been content with good will for the salvation of Israel to kiss the soles of his feet. But I did this, that I might not prefer the glory of man above the glory of God: neither will I worship any but thee, O God, neither will I do it in pride.”

It was not contempt and it was not pride. He would have kissed the soles of Aman's feet for the salvation of Israel. He refused so as not to set the glory of man above the glory of the Most High, and because he would worship none but the Most High.

That is why we do not bow. The three Hebrew children did not bow to the image in Babylon, Mordecai did not bow to Haman, and we pledge allegiance to none but the Most High.

precepts.text: Haman was full of wrath because Mardocheus bowed not, and he sought to destroy all the Jews throughout the kingdom, not Mardocheus alone.
precepts.point: This sounds exactly like the curses laid out for our people in Deuteronomy 28, where the enemy shows no favor toward the young or the old. Both the ancient and the present generation were marked for the grave in one day.

note.label: Esther 13: The Decree of Destruction and the Prayer of Mardocheus

precepts.why:
The letter goes out in the king's name, but the picture in it is Haman's. The canonical book shows where it began: “when Haman saw that Mordecai bowed not, nor did him reverence, then was Haman full of wrath.” He “thought scorn to lay hands on Mordecai alone; for they had shewed him the people of Mordecai: wherefore Haman sought to destroy all the Jews that were throughout the whole kingdom of Ahasuerus, even the people of Mordecai.”

One man would not bow, and Haman's wrath went out to a whole nation. That is why the letter is not about Mardocheus; it is about “a certain malicious people” scattered “in all nations throughout the world”, and why it commands that they “all, with their wives and children, be utterly destroyed by the sword of their enemies, without all mercy and pity”. The order is for the destruction of the Israelites, young and old together, because Haman scorned to lay hands on one alone.

precepts.text: Haman told the king of a people scattered abroad whose laws are diverse, offered ten thousand talents of silver, and the king gave him his ring to seal the decree.
precepts.point: This sounds exactly like the curses laid out for our people in Deuteronomy 28, where the enemy shows no favor toward the young or the old. Both the ancient and the present generation were marked for the grave in one day.

note.label: Esther 13: The Decree of Destruction and the Prayer of Mardocheus

precepts.why:
The slander in the letter is what Haman told the king. “There is a certain people scattered abroad and dispersed among the people in all the provinces of thy kingdom; and their laws are diverse from all people; neither keep they the king’s laws: therefore it is not for the king’s profit to suffer them.” The letter repeats it: a people “scattered”, with “laws contrary to all nations”, that “continually despised the commandments of kings”, and “this people alone is continually in opposition unto all men, differing in the strange manner of their laws”. Haman painted Israel as a mischievous, malicious nation so the uniting of the kingdoms could not go forward, and the letter carries his painting.

Then he bought it: “let it be written that they may be destroyed: and I will pay ten thousand talents of silver to the hands of those that have the charge of the business, to bring it into the king’s treasuries.” “And the king took his ring from his hand, and gave it unto Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, the Jews’ enemy.” That ring sealed the letter. That is why the ones to be destroyed are they that are “signified in writing unto you by Aman, who is ordained over the affairs, and is next unto us”: the Jews' enemy held the king's ring and wrote the decree.

precepts.text: The Most High foretold a nation of fierce countenance that would not regard the person of the old nor shew favour to the young.
precepts.point: This sounds exactly like the curses laid out for our people in Deuteronomy 28, where the enemy shows no favor toward the young or the old. Both the ancient and the present generation were marked for the grave in one day.

note.label: Esther 13: The Decree of Destruction and the Prayer of Mardocheus

precepts.why:
The decree marks all the Jews, “with their wives and children”, for the sword “without all mercy and pity”, so that “they, who of old and now also are malicious, may in one day with violence go into the grave”. The ancient and the present generation together, marked for the grave in one day.

That sounds exactly like the curses laid out for our people. “The Lord shall bring a nation against thee from far, from the end of the earth, as swift as the eagle flieth; a nation whose tongue thou shalt not understand; A nation of fierce countenance, which shall not regard the person of the old, nor shew favour to the young”. The Most High foretold an enemy that would show no favor toward the young or the old, and Haman's decree is that enemy: no mercy, no pity, wives and children with the men.

The letter is not only Persian history; it is the curse of Deuteronomy 28 falling on our people.

precepts.text: Mardocheus rent his clothes, put on sackcloth with ashes, went out into the city, and cried with a loud and bitter cry.
precepts.point: All Israel in like manner cried most earnestly unto the Lord because their death was before their eyes. Mardocheus rent his clothes and cried through the city with a loud and bitter cry, as the canonical account records.

note.label: Esther 13: The Decree of Destruction and the Prayer of Mardocheus

precepts.why:
The prayer of Mardocheus is what he prayed; the canonical book shows what he did. “When Mordecai perceived all that was done, Mordecai rent his clothes, and put on sackcloth with ashes, and went out into the midst of the city, and cried with a loud and a bitter cry”. The man who would not bow to proud Aman, and who told the Lord it “was neither in contempt nor pride, nor for any desire of glory”, went out into the midst of the city in sackcloth and ashes, crying aloud.

That loud and bitter cry is the “Hear my prayer” of the Apocrypha: “spare thy people: for their eyes are upon us to bring us to nought”. Their death was before their eyes, and Mardocheus cried it through the city as he cried it to the Most High.

precepts.text: In every province where the king's decree came there was great mourning among the Jews, with fasting and weeping and wailing, and many lay in sackcloth and ashes.
precepts.point: All Israel in like manner cried most earnestly unto the Lord because their death was before their eyes. Mardocheus rent his clothes and cried through the city with a loud and bitter cry, as the canonical account records.

note.label: Esther 13: The Decree of Destruction and the Prayer of Mardocheus

precepts.why:
“All Israel in like manner cried most earnestly unto the Lord, because their death was before their eyes.” The canonical book records it province by province: “in every province, whithersoever the king’s commandment and his decree came, there was great mourning among the Jews, and fasting, and weeping, and wailing; and many lay in sackcloth and ashes.”

It was not Mardocheus alone. Wherever the decree came, the whole nation mourned, fasted, wept and wailed, and many lay in sackcloth and ashes as he did. That is “All Israel in like manner”: a nation with death before its eyes crying most earnestly to the Most High to spare his people and turn their sorrow into joy.

points: This is the decree written against the Jews in the king's name. Aman, that excelled in wisdom among us, and was approved for his constant good will and steadfast fidelity, and had the honour of the second place in the kingdom: that is Haman.

Declared unto us, that in all nations throughout the world there was scattered a certain malicious people, that had laws contrary to all nations, and continually despised the commandments of kings: there is Haman slandering us, the same slander used on us today: they are malicious, they are violent, they are a problem.

So as the uniting of our kingdoms cannot go forward: Haman was a Macedonian Edomite in Persia, saying the kingdoms cannot unite as long as these Jews are around, this people alone, continually in opposition unto all men, working all the mischief they can that our kingdom may not be firmly established. The accuser's argument has not changed in all these ages.
